title: Rate + latency tomography suite for core engines
creator: Ava Lin
description: Build a durable, multi-mode microbenchmark suite ("Token Tomography") to characterize tokens-per-second and tail latency for our core serving models across realistic client patterns. This ticket covers the harness design, test artifacts, alerting integration, and a lightweight CI job to catch regressions to p95 and sustained TPS. The goal is to detect 10%+ regressions in p95 or 15%+ regressions in sustained TPS for any runtime change before it lands in canary.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible harness runnable locally and in CI that produces TPS and p50/p90/p95/p99 for a given model and config
Support for at least three client traffic shapes: bursty short-seq, steady medium-seq, and long-context steady-state
Automated warmup stage that primes the KV cache and measures cold-to-warm delta
Regression detector that compares current run to golden baseline and emits a pass/fail with percent delta thresholds
A lightweight GitHub Action/CI job that runs the harness for PRs touching runtime or kernel selection code and posts results to the PR
Prometheus metrics emitted for TPS and p95 with labels for model, quantization, batch_size, and route
Alerting rule in Alertmanager that triggers when p95 regression > 10% AND TPS drop > 15% for core model group
Documentation page with example runs, CLI flags, and how to add new client shapes or models
steps: Design harness CLI and YAML job spec: inputs = model, route, seq_distribution, concurrency_profile, duration
Create three canonical client profiles and store as JSON in repo: short_burst.json, steady_medium.json, long_context.json
Implement driver that can run N parallel clients across multiple worker machines and aggregate latency histograms using HDRHistogram
Add KV cache warmup routine to driver with configurable prefix set and perf-only mode
Wire outputs to a result artifact: gzipped HDR histogram + metadata JSON + condensed summary CSV
Implement regression detector util that compares current summary to baseline and returns JSON with percent deltas per-quantile
Create GH Action that spins up a small ephemeral dedicated pod in our test fleet, runs the short_burst profile for 3 minutes, and comments results on PR
Add Prometheus exporter that converts harness metrics into canonical metric names used by console dashboards
decisions: Use HDRHistogram (Java) for client-side quantile tracking to avoid percentile noise from aggregation
Baseline storage: keep golden baselines in S3 with timestamped versions and a 'pinned' tag per-model
CI mode: run a single 3-minute short_burst profile; scheduled nightly matrix job runs full sweep against pinned baselines
Alert threshold chosen conservatively: p95 delta 10% and TPS drop 15% to reduce noisy alerts while catching meaningful regressions
notes: We considered Rust client for low overhead but chose JVM driver for existing HDRHistogram ecosystem and integration speed
Will reuse existing load generator infra from ENG-34122 for multi-worker orchestration
Don't block landing on a partial harness — ship short_burst CI early and iterate on additional profiles
Coordinate with Console team to ensure metrics labels align with per-route breakdowns (PM: Elena Rodriguez)
Keep the golden baseline repo small; only store baselines for core model families to limit storage costs
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/314 (CI GH Action and ephemeral test pod spec)
blockers: Metric cardinality: need to finalize label set with Console to avoid high cardinality metrics
Test fleet quotas: ephemeral pods for CI runs require quota increase in us-west-2 (infra ticket open)
